subject: Priority gating & rollback criteria for SummitBank enterprise commitment
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, May 1, 2027 at 9:12 AM -0700
Subject: SummitBank: priority gating & rollout asks

Team —

Quick context: SummitBank (deal SB-2025-042) is asking for two product commitments to close their Q3 contract:

  1) Per-tenant continuous audit export (S3/secure transfer) with 90-day retention and configurable retention window per tenant.
  2) Per-route request tracing (trace_id propagation + per-request metadata) surfaced to our logs/observability (customer-facing view).

They've signaled urgency — commercial is at $1.2M ARR confirmed (see HubSpot link below). Legal/procurement want explicit rollout gating and rollback criteria spelled out in the SOW before they sign. Summit indicated they can accept a staged delivery (MVP + production rollout) but need commitments on timelines and a remedy if we miss milestones (credit or extended pilot).

Ask: can Product/Eng evaluate whether we can land an MVP for (1) and (2) within a 6-week window starting May 10? If not, propose the shortest viable scope we can commit to that materially unblocks the deal.

I've attached the mutual action plan they sent and a draft SLA to illustrate the gating language.

Attachments: SummitBank_MutualActionPlan.xlsx, SLA_Draft_v2.pdf

Next steps I'd like:
- Karthik: high-level scope/risks & whether a 6-week MVP is feasible.
- Jasmine: if Eng needs an enablement/POC tenant, CS can provision and drive acceptance tests.
- Monica: I'll need your customer-facing requirements summary (2–3 acceptance criteria) for the SOW.

We'd like a firm internal commitment by EOD Tue (May 4) so sales can respond to procurement.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

On May 1, 2027 at 09:12 AM Marissa attached: SummitBank_MutualActionPlan.xlsx (spreadsheet), SLA_Draft_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, May 3, 2027 at 08:34 AM -07:00
Subject: Re: SummitBank: priority gating & rollout asks

Marissa —

Thanks for the heads-up and the MAP. Quick read: both asks are reasonable from a product perspective, but there are clear engineering trade-offs. High level notes:

  - Per-tenant continuous export (streaming) is non-trivial: security (per-tenant creds/keying), throughput backpressure, and config-at-runtime support. Our baseline implementation (safe, auditable) will likely take ~10–12 weeks to complete with full SLAs.

  - MVP alternative: daily batched exports (S3 prefix per tenant) + single-tenant manual rotation of creds. That reduces work to ~4–6 weeks if we scope the MVP tightly: export, simple selector UI, and docs. It would not deliver low-latency streaming but meets many audit/compliance needs.

  - Per-route tracing: we can expose trace_id propagation and attach a request metadata blob to logs in ~3–4 weeks as an opt-in by-route feature. Surface to customer-facing logs (they can pull via export) should be doable within the same window as the batched export MVP. Full observability UI for customers would take longer.

Questions for clarity (will affect estimates):
  1) Do we need encryption-at-rest with customer-managed KMS for the exported data on day one?
  2) Is the retention policy (90 days) firm or negotiable to 60 days if it reduces complexity?
  3) Will Summit accept a staged SOW that has credits for missed milestones and a defined canary approach?

Given our current roadmap commitments (notable: two queued infra projects with firm dates), to prioritize this we need: deal commit signals (signed MSA or firm PO date) and Product prioritization from leadership. If Sales pushes for prioritization, we should document acceptance criteria and a rollback plan (what gets disabled/rolled back on failure).

I can scope an MVP tech plan and a JIRA EPIC by EOD Mon (May 4) if that's helpful.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | VP, Product Management | Redwood Inference

On Mon, May 3, 2027 at 08:34 AM Karthik attached: none

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, May 3, 2027 at 11:18 AM -07:00
Subject: Re: SummitBank: priority gating & rollout asks

Folks —

From CS perspective: SummitBank's compliance and ops teams will not accept a solution that is "partial" for long. Their core ask is reproducible, auditable export and an observability trail for every request tied to a trace id so they can reconcile behavior across services.

Operational appetite: they will run acceptance tests and validate with our test tenant (we can set this up). They're willing to sign a staged SOW with milestone definitions if we can provide firm dates for an MVP and a canary that enables up to 10% of traffic for their users.

Commercial context (for prioritization):
  - ARR: $1.2M first-year committed, with expansion potential to $2.8M over 24 months per the AE.
  - Procurement is flexible on payment timing if we give them deterministic rollout milestones and a penalty clause for missed dates (service credit / free pilot months).

If Product signs off on the batched-export + trace_id MVP, CS will run acceptance criteria design with Summit this week and own the UAT. We'll also provide a prioritized list of three user journeys they must be able to reconcile post-delivery.

Monica
Monica Patel | Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

On Mon, May 3, 2027 at 11:18 AM Monica attached: none

From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@summitbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@procurement.summitbank.com>, SummitBank Legal <legal@summitbank.com>
Date: Mon, May 3, 2027 at 13:45 -04:00
Subject: Re: SummitBank: priority gating & rollout asks

Marissa & team —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Procurement here — we are prepared to accept staged delivery if Redwood can commit to milestone dates and remedies. Our product/security teams will validate using the test tenant Monica referenced.

Two clarifications from our side:
  1) KMS: we prefer customer-managed keys for the exported artifacts but could accept Redwood-managed KMS for the initial pilot if we retain the option to migrate keys within 30 days.
  2) Acceptable remedy: we are asking for a contractual 3% ARR service credit for each week past a committed milestone up to a maximum of 12% unless mutually agreed remediation is in place.

I've attached the MAP with our proposed milestone dates — please review and respond with any changes. We can sign an amendment to the SOW to reflect staged acceptance.

Thanks —
Lisa Chen
Head of Platform Integrations | SummitBank

On Mon, May 3, 2027 at 01:45 PM Lisa attached: SummitBank_MutualActionPlan.xlsx

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, May 4, 2027 at 16:04 -07:00
Subject: Re: SummitBank: priority gating & rollout asks

Thanks everyone — good thread. Quick summary and next moves from GTM: 

  - Commercial: Sales can hold signature if Product gives a firm MVP commitment and gating language for the SOW. Summit is willing to sign a staged SOW + PO.
  - Product ask: can we commit to a batched-export MVP + trace_id propagation for a 6-week target starting May 10, with a canary (5–10% traffic) for production validation? If not, give us the earliest realistic timeline and a minimal scope we can promise.
  - Remediation: if Product cannot meet the target, Sales is authorized to offer up to 3 months of free pilot support + a limited service credit (negotiable per counsel) to keep momentum.

Karthik — please confirm:
  1) Whether Eng can produce a high-level engineering plan (EPIC + rough story points) by EOD Tue (May 4).
  2) Whether we can agree on canary gating criteria (metrics and rollback triggers).

Monica/Jasmine — please be ready to run UAT and acceptance tests once Eng provides ETA. I'll coordinate commercial language with Legal to draft the amendment.

If Product signs off, I'll schedule a joint review with Summit for Wed (May 5).

—Sean
Sean Gallagher | Head of Sales, North America | Redwood Inference
